title: Prakrama 2, Sarga 5. The Telling of Ecstasy
html:
The Lord goes with His devotees to Advaita in Shantipura; Their meeting; a discourse on bhakti in the Kali age; a non-Vaishnava at the festival; pastimes in Advaita's house; instruction in jnana-yoga and the praise of pure devotion

Verse 1

ततो जगाम पुर्यां स श्रीवासादिभिरन्वितः।
अद्वैताचार्यवर्यस्य भक्तस्य दर्शनोत्सुकः॥१॥

tato jagāma puryāṁ sa śrīvāsādibhiranvitaḥ|
advaitācāryavaryasya bhaktasya darśanotsukaḥ||1||

tatah — then; jagama — went; puryam — to the town; sah — He; shrivasa-adibhih — by Srivasa and others; anvitah — accompanied; advaita-acharya-varyasya — of Advaita, the best of acharyas; bhaktasya — of the devotee; darshana-utsukah — eager for the sight.

1Then, accompanied by Srivasa and others, He set out for the town, eager to see His devotee Advaita, the best of acharyas.

Verse 2

गच्छन्पथि मुहुर्गायन्हरेर्गीतं मुदान्वितः।
क्वचिन्नृत्यति नृत्यद्भिः स्वजनैः सह स प्रभुः॥२॥

gacchanpathi muhurgāyanharergītaṁ mudānvitaḥ|
kvacinnṛtyati nṛtyadbhiḥ svajanaiḥ saha sa prabhuḥ||2||

gachchhan — going; pathi — on the road; muhuh — again and again; gayan — singing; hareh — of Hari; gitam — a song; muda-anvitah — joyful; kvachit — at times; nrityati — dances; nrityadbhih — dancing; svajanaih saha — with His own people; sah — that; prabhuh — Lord.

2On the way the Lord, full of joy, sang songs of Hari again and again, and at times He broke into dance together with His own people, who danced as well.

Verse 3

ततो गत्वा पपातोर्व्यामाचार्यस्य समीपतः।
दण्डवद्वैष्णवं विष्णुं मन्यमानोऽनुशिक्षयन्॥३॥

tato gatvā papātorvyāmācāryasya samīpataḥ|
daṇḍavadvaiṣṇavaṁ viṣṇuṁ manyamāno'nuśikṣayan||3||

tatah — then; gatva — having come; papata — fell; urvyam — on the earth; acharyasya — of the Acharya; samipatah — near; dandavat — like a stick; vaishnavam — a Vaishnava; vishnum — as Vishnu; manyamanah — regarding; anushikshayan — teaching.

3On arriving, He fell to the earth like a stick before the Acharya: regarding a Vaishnava as Vishnu Himself, He taught this to others.

Verse 4

तं दृष्ट्वा सहसोत्थायाचार्यस्तु तत्समीपतः।
गत्वा पपात भूमौ स सम्भ्रमेण जगद्गुरुः॥४॥

taṁ dṛṣṭvā sahasotthāyācāryastu tatsamīpataḥ|
gatvā papāta bhūmau sa sambhrameṇa jagadguruḥ||4||

tam — Him; drishtva — seeing; sahasa — at once; utthaya — rising; acharyah — the Acharya; tu — and; tat-samipatah — near Him; gatva — going; papata — fell; bhumau — on the ground; sah — he; sambhramena — in reverent agitation; jagat-guruh — the teacher of the world.

4Seeing Him, the Acharya, the teacher of the world, at once rose, came up to Him in reverent agitation, and He too fell to the ground.

Verse 5

अन्योन्यालिङ्गनं कृत्वा प्रेमोत्कण्ठौ बभूवतुः।
कम्पाश्रुपुलकाद्यैस्तु परिपूर्णस्वविग्रहौ॥५॥

anyonyāliṅganaṁ kṛtvā premotkaṇṭhau babhūvatuḥ|
kampāśrupulakādyaistu paripūrṇasvavigrahau||5||

anyonya-alinganam — a mutual embrace; kritva — having made; prema-utkanthau — longing in love; babhuvatuh — both became; kampa-ashru-pulaka-adyaih — with trembling, tears, thrilling of the hair and the rest; tu — and; paripurna-sva-vigrahau — their bodies filled.

5They clasped each other in an embrace, and both were seized by the longing of love: Their bodies were filled with trembling, tears, the thrill of the hair and the other signs of ecstasy.

Verse 6

उपविश्य ततो देवः कथां चक्रे हरेः प्रियाम्।
मनोहरां पापहरां मुक्तिप्रेमफलप्रदाम्॥६॥

upaviśya tato devaḥ kathāṁ cakre hareḥ priyām|
manoharāṁ pāpaharāṁ muktipremaphalapradām||6||

upavishya — sitting; tatah — then; devah — the Lord; katham — a discourse; chakre — made; hareh — about Hari; priyam — dear; manoharam — captivating the mind; papa-haram — taking away sin; mukti-prema-phala-pradam — bestowing the fruits of liberation and love.

6Then, sitting down, the Lord began a heart-endearing discourse on Hari — captivating the mind, taking away sin, bestowing the fruits of liberation and love.

Verse 7

ततोऽद्वैतोऽब्रवीद्वाक्यं भक्तिर्नास्ति कलौ क्षितौ।
इति मूढा वदन्ते ये ते पश्यन्त्वद्य चक्षुषा॥७॥

tato'dvaito'bravīdvākyaṁ bhaktirnāsti kalau kṣitau|
iti mūḍhā vadante ye te paśyantvadya cakṣuṣā||7||

tatah — then; advaitah — Advaita; abravit — spoke; vakyam — a word; bhaktih — devotion; na asti — there is no; kalau — in Kali; kshitau — on earth; iti — thus; mudhah — fools; vadante — say; ye — who; te — they; pashyantu — let them see; adya — today; chakshusha — with their eyes.

7Advaita then said: "Those fools who claim that in the Kali age there is no devotion on earth — let them see it today with their own eyes!"

Verse 8

तच्छ्रुत्वा भगवानाह किञ्चित्प्रस्फुरिताधरः।
भक्तिश्चेन्नास्ति नृहरेः किं तदास्ति क्षिताविह॥८॥

tacchrutvā bhagavānāha kiñcitprasphuritādharaḥ|
bhaktiścennāsti nṛhareḥ kiṁ tadāsti kṣitāviha||8||

tat — that; shrutva — hearing; bhagavan — Bhagavan; aha — said; kinchit — slightly; prasphurita-adharah — His lips trembling; bhaktih — devotion; chet — if; na asti — there is not; nrihareh — to Nrihari; kim — what; tada — then; asti — is there; kshitau — on earth; iha — here.

8Hearing this, Bhagavan, His lips trembling slightly, said: "If there is no devotion to Nrihari, what then is there at all, here on earth?

Verse 9

भक्तिरेवास्ति संसारे सर्वसारा सुखावहा।
सा नास्तीति च यो ब्रूते जन्म तस्य निरर्थकम्॥९॥

bhaktirevāsti saṁsāre sarvasārā sukhāvahā|
sā nāstīti ca yo brūte janma tasya nirarthakam||9||

bhaktih — devotion; eva — alone; asti — is; samsare — in the world; sarva-sara — the essence of all; sukha-avaha — bringing happiness; sa — it; na asti — is not; iti — that; cha — and; yah — who; brute — says; janma — birth; tasya — his; nirarthakam — meaningless.

9Devotion alone exists in this world — the essence of all, the bringer of happiness. And whoever says that it does not exist has been born in vain.

Verse 10

तस्मात्कृष्णे भक्तिरास्ते सुप्रसन्ना सनातनी।
यस्य स्यात्कर्मबन्धश्च नश्येत्प्रेमा हरौ भवेत्॥१०॥

tasmātkṛṣṇe bhaktirāste suprasannā sanātanī|
yasya syātkarmabandhaśca naśyetpremā harau bhavet||10||

tasmat — therefore; krishne — for Krishna; bhaktih — devotion; aste — abides; su-prasanna — serene; sanatani — eternal; yasya — whose; syat — it may be; karma-bandhah — the bondage of karma; cha — and; nashyet — will perish; prema — love; harau — for Hari; bhavet — will arise.

10And so devotion to Krishna abides — serene and eternal; and for one who has it, the bonds of karma fall away and love for Hari is born."

Verse 11

ततोऽवदच्छ्रीनिवासो दृष्ट्वा कञ्चिदवैष्णवम्।
द्विजं प्रस्फुटमेवाग्रे हरेः संसदि दुःखितः॥११॥

tato'vadacchrīnivāso dṛṣṭvā kañcidavaiṣṇavam|
dvijaṁ prasphuṭamevāgre hareḥ saṁsadi duḥkhitaḥ||11||

tatah — then; avadat — said; shrinivasah — Srinivasa; drishtva — seeing; kanchit — a certain; avaishnavam — non-Vaishnava; dvijam — brahmana; prasphutam eva — quite plainly; agre — in front; hareh — of Hari; samsadi — in the assembly; duhkhitah — grieved.

11Then Srinivasa, noticing in Hari's assembly, right in front, a certain brahmana who was plainly no Vaishnava, said in distress:

Verse 12

विघ्नं कृष्णोत्सवे कर्तुं द्विजोऽयं समुपागतः।
तच्छ्रुत्वा भगवान्प्राह नायमत्रागमिष्यति॥१२॥

vighnaṁ kṛṣṇotsave kartuṁ dvijo'yaṁ samupāgataḥ|
tacchrutvā bhagavānprāha nāyamatrāgamiṣyati||12||

vighnam — obstruction; krishna-utsave — in Krishna's festival; kartum — to make; dvijah — brahmana; ayam — this; samupagatah — has come; tat — that; shrutva — hearing; bhagavan — Bhagavan; praha — said; na — not; ayam — he; atra — here; agamishyati — will come.

12"This brahmana has come to disrupt Krishna's festival." Hearing this, Bhagavan replied: "He will not come in here.

Verse 13

नास्त्यत्र तव विप्रेन्द्र चिन्ता काचित्सुखी भव।
नायातस्तत्र विप्रोऽसौ विष्णुमायाविमोहितः॥१३॥

nāstyatra tava viprendra cintā kācitsukhī bhava|
nāyātastatra vipro'sau viṣṇumāyāvimohitaḥ||13||

na asti — there is not; atra — in this; tava — for you; vipra-indra — O best of brahmanas; chinta — anxiety; kachit — any; sukhi — happy; bhava — be; na — not; ayatah — has come; tatra — there; viprah — brahmana; asau — that; vishnu-maya-vimohitah — bewildered by Vishnu's maya.

13Have no anxiety over this, O best of brahmanas; be happy: bewildered by Vishnu's maya, that brahmana has not come here at all."

Verse 14

स्वयं शान्तिपुरं गत्वा दृष्ट्वाद्वैतमहेश्वरम्।
ऐश्वर्यं कथयन्कृष्णपूर्णावेशो बभूव ह॥१४॥

svayaṁ śāntipuraṁ gatvā dṛṣṭvādvaitamaheśvaram|
aiśvaryaṁ kathayankṛṣṇapūrṇāveśo babhūva ha||14||

svayam — Himself; shantipuram — to Shantipura; gatva — having gone; drishtva — having seen; advaita-maheshvaram — Advaita, the great lord; aishvaryam — majesty; kathayan — telling; krishna-purna-aveshah — wholly possessed by Krishna; babhuva — became; ha — indeed.

14Having come Himself to Shantipura and seen Advaita, the great lord1, the Lord, telling of Krishna's majesty, was wholly filled with Him.

Verse 15

ततः क्रीडापरो भूत्वा श्रीवासस्यांसदेशके।
दत्त्वा सव्ये सव्यबाहुं वामं प्रादाद्गदाधरे॥१५॥

tataḥ krīḍāparo bhūtvā śrīvāsasyāṁsadeśake|
dattvā savye savyabāhuṁ vāmaṁ prādādgadādhare||15||

tatah — then; krida-parah — intent on play; bhutva — becoming; shrivasasya — of Srivasa; amsa-deshake — on the shoulder; dattva — placing; savye — on the right; savya-bahum — His right arm; vamam — the left; pradat — placed; gadadhare — on Gadadhara.

15Then, given over to play, He laid His right arm on Srivasa's right shoulder and His left on Gadadhara;

Verse 16

श्रीरामपण्डितस्याङ्के दत्त्वा पादाम्बुजं हरिः।
तैः सार्धं मुमुदे श्रीमदद्वैताचार्यसन्निधौ॥१६॥

śrīrāmapaṇḍitasyāṅke dattvā pādāmbujaṁ hariḥ|
taiḥ sārdhaṁ mumude śrīmadadvaitācāryasannidhau||16||

shri-rama-panditasya — of Sri Rama Pandita; anke — on the lap; dattva — placing; pada-ambujam — His lotus feet; harih — Hari; taih sardham — with them; mumude — rejoiced; shrimat-advaita-acharya-sannidhau — in the presence of Srimad Advaita Acharya.

16placing His lotus feet in the lap of Sri Rama Pandita2, Hari rejoiced with them in the presence of Srimad Advaita Acharya.

Verse 17

तत्र भुक्त्वा वरान्नं स चन्दनेनानुलेप्य च।
गात्राणि हर्षयँल्लोकं जगौ कृष्णं ननर्त च॥१७॥

tatra bhuktvā varānnaṁ sa candanenānulepya ca|
gātrāṇi harṣaya~llokaṁ jagau kṛṣṇaṁ nanarta ca||17||

tatra — there; bhuktva — having eaten; vara-annam — choice food; sah — He; chandanena — with sandal paste; anulepya — having anointed; cha — and; gatrani — His limbs; harshayan — delighting; lokam — the people; jagau — sang of; krishnam — Krishna; nanarta — danced; cha — and.

17There He ate choice food, anointed His limbs with sandal paste, and, delighting the people, sang of Krishna and danced.

Verse 18

आचार्यो बुबुधे पूर्णमात्मानमाशिषा बुधः।
दृष्ट्वा श्रीगौरचन्द्रस्य प्रेमानन्दमहोत्सवम्॥१८॥

ācāryo bubudhe pūrṇamātmānamāśiṣā budhaḥ|
dṛṣṭvā śrīgauracandrasya premānandamahotsavam||18||

acharyah — the Acharya; bubudhe — deemed; purnam — fulfilled; atmanam — himself; ashisha — by the blessing; budhah — the wise; drishtva — seeing; shri-gaurachandrasya — of Sri Gaurachandra; prema-ananda-maha-utsavam — the great festival of the bliss of love.

18The wise Acharya, beholding the great festival of Sri Gaurachandra's bliss of love, felt Himself fulfilled by grace.

Verse 19

आचार्येण समं कृष्णः कीर्तयन्स जगद्गुरुः।
क्रीडित्वा देववत्तत्र पुनरागान्निजालयम्॥१९॥

ācāryeṇa samaṁ kṛṣṇaḥ kīrtayansa jagadguruḥ|
krīḍitvā devavattatra punarāgānnijālayam||19||

acharyena samam — together with the Acharya; krishnah — Krishna; kirtayan — performing kirtana; sah — He; jagat-guruh — the Teacher of the world; kriditva — having played; deva-vat — like a god; tatra — there; punah — again; agat — returned; nija-alayam — to His own home.

19Krishna, the Teacher of the world, having performed kirtana with the Acharya and engaged there in divine play, then returned to His own home.

Verse 20

ततः सोऽध्यात्मतत्त्वार्थं वक्तुमारेभ ईश्वरः।
एक एव हरिः स्वामी व्यष्टिरूपतया स्थितः॥२०॥

tataḥ so'dhyātmatattvārthaṁ vaktumārebha īśvaraḥ|
eka eva hariḥ svāmī vyaṣṭirūpatayā sthitaḥ||20||

tatah — then; sah — He; adhyatma-tattva-artham — the meaning of the truth of the Self; vaktum — to expound; arebhe — began; ishvarah — the Lord; ekah — one; eva — alone; harih — Hari; svami — the master; vyashti-rupataya — in the form of individuals; sthitah — abides.

20Afterwards the Lord began to expound the meaning of the truth of the Self:3 "Hari alone is the master, and He abides in the form of individual beings.

Verse 21

संहृतः स्वयमेवैकस्तिष्ठत्यात्मा स्वयं प्रभुः।
सर्वस्यान्तर्बहिः साक्षी कारणानां च कारणम्॥२१॥

saṁhṛtaḥ svayamevaikastiṣṭhatyātmā svayaṁ prabhuḥ|
sarvasyāntarbahiḥ sākṣī kāraṇānāṁ ca kāraṇam||21||

samhritah — having withdrawn (all) into Himself; svayam eva — Himself; ekah — alone; tishthati — remains; atma — the Self; svayam — Himself; prabhuh — the Lord; sarvasya — of everything; antah — within; bahih — without; sakshi — the witness; karananam — of causes; cha — and; karanam — the cause.

21Having withdrawn all into Himself, He remains alone — the Self, the Lord Himself, the witness of all within and without, the cause of all causes."

Verse 22

इति हस्तं प्रसार्याशु मुष्टीकृत्य स्वयं पुनः।
करं स दर्शयामास नृत्यन्निव स ईश्वरः॥२२॥

iti hastaṁ prasāryāśu muṣṭīkṛtya svayaṁ punaḥ|
karaṁ sa darśayāmāsa nṛtyanniva sa īśvaraḥ||22||

iti — so (saying); hastam — His hand; prasarya — opening; ashu — quickly; mushtikritya — clenching into a fist; svayam — Himself; punah — again; karam — the hand; sah — He; darshayam asa — showed; nrityan iva — as if dancing; sah — that; ishvarah — Lord.

22So saying, the Lord quickly opened His hand, then Himself clenched it again into a fist, and showed His hand as if in a dance4.

Verse 23

पुनरूचे वचस्तत्त्वं सत्तामात्रस्वरूपिणम्।
भावोऽप्यनर्थकस्तत्र सद्रूपमवधार्यताम्॥२३॥

punarūce vacastattvaṁ sattāmātrasvarūpiṇam|
bhāvo'pyanarthakastatra sadrūpamavadhāryatām||23||

punah — again; uche — spoke; vachah — words; tattvam — on the truth; satta-matra-svarupinam — (on Him) whose nature is pure being; bhavah — becoming; api — even; anarthakah — meaningless; tatra — there; sat-rupam — the form of the Real; avadharyatam — let it be grasped.

23Again He spoke of the truth — of Him whose nature is pure being: "There even becoming is meaningless; grasp the Real.

Verse 24

एकत्वं ब्रह्मणोऽपि स्यादेवं मूर्तिर्न सर्वथा।
अन्यस्य मूर्तिर्भवति विना तज्ज्ञानकारणात्॥२४॥

ekatvaṁ brahmaṇo'pi syādevaṁ mūrtirna sarvathā|
anyasya mūrtirbhavati vinā tajjñānakāraṇāt||24||

ekatvam — oneness; brahmanah — of Brahman; api — indeed; syat — there is; evam — thus; murtih — a form; na — not; sarvatha — at all; anyasya — of another; murtih — a form; bhavati — arises; vina — without; tat-jnana-karanat — because of (lacking) that knowledge.

24Brahman is one; therefore there is no other form at all. The form of 'another' arises only from the lack of this knowledge.

Verse 25

पश्याङ्गुली करस्थे मे ह्येका तत्र मधुप्लुता।
जिह्वया तां लिहस्वाद्य तदन्या पूयसंप्लुता॥२५॥

paśyāṅgulī karasthe me hyekā tatra madhuplutā|
jihvayā tāṁ lihasvādya tadanyā pūyasaṁplutā||25||

pashya — see; anguli — two fingers; kara-sthe — on the hand; me — My; hi — for; eka — one; tatra — of them; madhu-pluta — smeared with honey; jihvaya — with the tongue; tam — it; lihasva — lick; adya — now; tat — but; anya — the other; puya-sampluta — smeared with pus.

25Look at these two fingers of My hand: one is smeared with honey — lick it with your tongue; but the other is smeared with pus.

Verse 26

तां दृष्ट्वा घृणया चान्यं द्रष्टुं नोत्सहते क्षणम्।
निर्भेदब्रह्मज्ञानाद्धि सर्वमेव सुलक्षणम्॥२६॥

tāṁ dṛṣṭvā ghṛṇayā cānyaṁ draṣṭuṁ notsahate kṣaṇam|
nirbhedabrahmajñānāddhi sarvameva sulakṣaṇam||26||

tam — it; drishtva — seeing; ghrinaya — from disgust; cha — and; anyam — at the other; drashtum — to look; na utsahate — cannot bear; kshanam — for a moment; nirbheda-brahma-jnanat — from the knowledge of Brahman without distinctions; hi — but; sarvam eva — everything; su-lakshanam — is of auspicious mark.

26Seeing that one, you cannot in your disgust bear to look at the other even for a moment. Yet to one who knows Brahman without distinctions, everything is fair.

Verse 27

एवमेकोऽपि भगवाननादिः पुरुषोऽव्ययः।
सामग्रीरसतो जीवो मुक्तो भवति नान्यथा॥२७॥

evameko'pi bhagavānanādiḥ puruṣo'vyayaḥ|
sāmagrīrasato jīvo mukto bhavati nānyathā||27||

Verse 28

एवं बहुप्रकारं स ज्ञानयोगं दयानिधिः।
उक्त्वा तु विररामार्यहृदयस्थपदाम्बुजः॥२८॥

evaṁ bahuprakāraṁ sa jñānayogaṁ dayānidhiḥ|

Verse 29

श्रावयित्वा ततो ज्ञानं ज्ञानगम्यं जगत्पतिम्।

śrāvayitvā tato jñānaṁ jñānagamyaṁ jagatpatim|

भक्तिरेव समुत्कृष्टा कृष्णप्रेमप्रकाशिनी।

bhaktireva samutkṛṣṭā kṛṣṇapremaprakāśinī|
ityevāha sadotkaṇṭho gadgadaṁ jagadīśvaraḥ||30||

bhaktih — devotion; eva — alone; samutkrishta — supreme; krishna-prema-prakashini — revealing love for Krishna; iti — thus; eva — indeed; aha — said; sada-utkanthah — ever longing; gadgadam — in a faltering voice; jagat-ishvarah — the Lord of the world.

Verse 31

प्रेमाश्रुकण्ठो भगवानिदं वचनमब्रवीत्।

31His throat choked with tears of love, Bhagavan spoke these words: "His heart melted, his speech faltering, My devotee weeps freely, and laughs,

Verse 32

नृत्यत्यलं गायति च मद्भक्तो भुवनत्रयम्।

nṛtyatyalaṁ gāyati ca madbhakto bhuvanatrayam|
punāti pāti satataṁ sarvāpadbhyo divāniśam||32||

nrityati — dances; alam — abundantly; gayati — sings; cha — and; mat-bhaktah — My devotee; bhuvana-trayam — the three worlds; punati — purifies; pati — protects; satatam — constantly; sarva-apadbhyah — from all calamities; diva-nisham — day and night.

Verse 33

इत्युक्त्वा हृष्टमनसा ननर्त स्वजनैः सह।

ityuktvā hṛṣṭamanasā nanarta svajanaiḥ saha|
śrīmadviśvambharo devo nijabhaktiprakāśakaḥ||33||

iti — thus; uktva — having spoken; hrishta-manasa — with a joyful heart; nanarta — danced; svajanaih saha — with His own people; shrimat-vishvambharah — Sriman Vishvambhara; devah — the Lord; nija-bhakti-prakashakah — the revealer of devotion to Himself.

Thus ends the fifth sarga, "The Telling of Ecstasy" (Bhava-kathana), of the second prakrama of the great poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. Advaita Acharya is revered as a descent of Maha-Vishnu, one with Sadashiva; hence the epithet "great lord" (maheshvara).
  2. Sri Rama Pandita (Ramai) is Srivasa's younger brother.
  3. Verses 20–27 expound jnana-yoga, the path of knowledge (cf. v. 28), as those who seek liberation understand it. The Lord expounds it in order to show its limit: at once, remembering Krishna's feet, He proclaims that devotion alone, which reveals love for Krishna, is supreme (vv. 29–32); cf. 2.04.22–23, where He tells Murari to give up his song on the doctrine of the Self. For a Gaudiya Vaishnava, the "oneness of Brahman" (v. 24) means that nothing exists apart from or independent of the Lord (vv. 20–21) — not that His form and the eternal soul dissolve into the impersonal: in v. 27, too, Bhagavan is called the beginningless, imperishable Person. This is not the Lord's final conclusion: the path of knowledge without devotion He rejects (cf. 2.06.23–26, where He forbids speaking of adhyatma, or prema will not be given).
  4. The opened palm and clenched fist depict the manifestation of the world and its withdrawal into the Lord.
  5. Literally, "from the taste of the totality" (samagri-rasa); the sense is unclear and the translation tentative.
  6. Cf. Bhagavata Purana 11.14.24, where Krishna likewise describes the devotee who purifies the world.
